notes:
Passed the fake-backend gate: G1-G5 and G9 pass; G6, G7 and G8 report only warnings; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null): no hardware was attached or run and no upstream Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab run was made. The card's entry symbol is the configuration class RoughWoStateEstimationEnvCfg; the registered environment class is isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv, which is outside the clone, so native is exactly the card's symbol and the fake models the Gymnasium environment interface that the external Isaac Lab base provides. The served task is Booster-T1-MotionTracking-v0 for the 23-DoF T1. The card's family-config/GymnasiumDriver shape was confirmed against the clone, so there is no deviation from the card.

The fake (fake.py) is pure Python: a 23-element unbounded action array, a 124-element flat placeholder observation (5 * 23 + 9), a seeded reset drawing joint offsets from the configured -0.1 to 0.1, a zero placeholder reward, terminated=False, and truncation at 500 control steps. The action length follows T1_CSV_JOINT_NAMES (motion_joint_names.py:28-52) and T1_23dof.urdf (booster_t1.py:25); the observation layout follows tracking_env_cfg.py:119-134 with motion_anchor_pos_b and base_lin_vel disabled by the T1 rough configuration (env_cfg.py:42-46); the 500-step truncation follows episode_length_s 10.0, decimation 4 and sim.dt 0.005 (tracking_env_cfg.py:325-328). No action bound is declared because the clone states none, only the unitless T1_ACTION_SCALE (booster_t1.py:128-168), so the bridge derives an unbounded array and enforces its length; this is why G8 reports SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE.

NOT COVERED: the Isaac Sim/PhysX dynamics, actuator and contact model, reward terms, termination terms and observation noise are not modelled; the T1 URDF and the t1_dance.npz motion NPZ (both in the external booster_assets repository) are not in the clone, so the fake's 23-element action vector and 124-element observation are placeholder shapes and its values are placeholders; the fake was never compared with an upstream run; the sim backend (gymnasium.make on a real Isaac Lab install) was not run. Real deployment is delegated to the separate booster_deploy repository (README.md:63).

Expected warnings kept from the last gate run: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x5 for the Gymnasium environment interface (action_space, observation_space, reset, step, close) whose implementation is outside the clone; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because no limit is declared; and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived inputs seed (reset), seed (seed class), ticks and action.values[*]. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. Only catalogue classes cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue_requests; no native.py, site-limits.example.json or fixtures/conformance.json is needed. test_driver.py keeps the required check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (action array length, step integration, seeded trajectory, seed class, 500-step truncation, unbounded values with length enforcement, published fidelity, e-stop latch); they pass. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
